page.layout: Running head centred at top, with the printed page number 348 at top right. One text column, with marginal notes in the right margin beside the last paragraph. Below the text: the catchword "Ver-" at right and the signature "R 5" at left.

main_text.p: tio, apud Deum non ex eorum nume-ro est, quæ à sola ipsius voluntate pen-dent: sed ad alia etiam relationem ha-bet, & in ipsa non de Deus tantum, sed de alternis quoq; jure agitur.

Ut igitur Deus neminem punit eam solam ob causam, quia sic velit, sed etiam, quia sic puniri meretur: Sic nemini imputat peccata aliena, quia simpliciter ita velit; sed quia is, ut sibi imputentur, commeritus fuerit. Et quemadmodum, ut quis verè puniri pos-sit, non satis est, quod ipse puniri velit, nisi delictum aliquod commiserit (Relativa enim sunt pœna & delictum; ita ut ubi delictum non est, ibi pœna esse nullo modo possit.) Sic ut alicui aliena peccata verè possint imputari, non satis est ipsum ita velle: nisi imputationis antecedens alia digna causa subsit, &c.
main_text.head: RESPONSIO.
main_text.p: Opponitur isti ratio-cinationi1. Idem sane tecum affirmare non dubitarem, si rationis & justitiæ ductum sequi tantum vellem, nisi ipsum Dei

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment ("tio,") cut at the column edge; kept as printed. The marginal note at the foot of the right margin is partly illegible: "Opponitur isti ratio-cinationi" is read, and the following word of the second line ("ora-") is uncertain. Several faint marks in the lower right margin are stains or show-through and are not transcribed. The signature after "R" is read as "5", with the second character uncertain. Dei and Deus are in small capitals in the print. The page's text ends mid-paragraph with "nisi ipsum Dei" and continues on the next page.
